ticketSource: Synthetic SIM-* issues only; no real Jira read/write.
repository: Disposable seeded local Git repositories; no Conductor checkout or remote writes.

scenarios.title: Small coding ticket
scenarios.coordinator: separate process in every execution scenario
scenarios.brief: Fix a whitespace normalization bug in a disposable TypeScript utility. Accept empty input and preserve internal spaces.
steps: Import synthetic Jira issue and explicitly choose the fixture repository.
Use scripted triage, apply a known patch in a worktree, run real local tests and independent scripted review.
Create a fake-provider PR, record synthetic hosted success and Jira progress.
scenarios.expected: One owned worktree, one fake PR, matching head/base evidence, criteria covered, readiness true and no merge write.

scenarios.title: Complex feature with selected specialists
scenarios.coordinator: separate process in every execution scenario
scenarios.brief: Add saved-filter export to a synthetic app, with empty-state behavior, input validation and an updated user guide.
steps: Accept three explicit criteria after optional Grill.
Schedule the selected specialists, apply staged code/docs patches under one writer lease, and run real unit/browser checks once the fixture app exists.
Reconcile each criterion with check/review evidence before fake PR readiness.
scenarios.expected: Up to three compatible specialists, one writer, all criteria linked to current artifacts; distinct configured models observed throughout.

scenarios.title: Failed checks and review cause bounded rework
scenarios.coordinator: separate process in every execution scenario
scenarios.brief: Fix pagination with an initially wrong boundary condition supplied by the scripted implementer.
steps: Apply the failing patch; execute real failing tests and return a scripted blocking review finding.
Supply a corrected patch and require fresh tests/review for the new SHA.
Run a variant with a third automatic repair request after two unsuccessful cycles.
scenarios.expected: Failure never reaches readiness; corrected current evidence can pass; exhausted recovery requires attention.

scenarios.title: Specialist and controller interruption
scenarios.coordinator: separate process in every execution scenario
scenarios.brief: Continue the small bug ticket after process failure while messages and local work are in flight.
steps: Kill specialist 2 after inbox persistence and before acknowledgement; independently restart or replace it.
In a separate variant, kill the coordinator after the external send committed but before its reply was recorded.
Reopen durable state and replay pending delivery with duplicate and stale-attempt messages.
scenarios.expected: Other processes remain observable; existing edits and receipts survive; one logical effect per action; uncertain outcomes stop rather than repeat blindly.

scenarios.title: Operator steering, insertion and pause
scenarios.coordinator: separate process in every execution scenario
scenarios.brief: While implementing input parsing, require a stricter accepted character set and insert a security specialist.
steps: Store operator steering while the coordinator is disconnected; then reconnect and record receipt/disposition.
Insert the specialist at a safe point; pause while a bounded child tool runs.
Reload and resume with the revised accepted brief.
scenarios.expected: Stored/received/applied are distinct; pausing lasts until child work stops; old-scope evidence is stale; new assignment and all history survive reload.

scenarios.title: Uncertain Jira and PR publication
scenarios.coordinator: separate process in every execution scenario
scenarios.brief: Publish the small ticket while fake Jira and Bitbucket lose responses.
steps: Make the fake provider commit one comment and one PR, then drop each response.
Restart Crewroom and return existing, reliably absent and inconclusive readback in separate variants.
Restore service and reconcile pending actions.
scenarios.expected: Exactly one PR/comment per logical action; uncertainty stays visible and blocks blind retry; accepted code work is preserved.

scenarios.title: Queue and merge dependencies
scenarios.coordinator: separate process in every execution scenario
scenarios.brief: Queue an independent fix and a dependent follow-up behind the first ticket.
steps: Change Jira rank and local queue order independently.
Hold the first fake PR in CI pending, then ready; verify release of independent work only.
Simulate closed-unmerged and later verified human merge for the dependency.
scenarios.expected: No overlap of coding tickets; no automatic backlog work; dependency only proceeds after observed merge; no merge API request.

scenarios.title: Routing failure, fallback and wrong model
scenarios.coordinator: separate process in every execution scenario
scenarios.brief: Process the same fixture ticket with failures at model preflight and provider response boundaries.
steps: Reject unsupported effort and missing pinned selectors before launch.
Inject 429 then recover; separately exercise a policy-approved alternate-model attempt and an unavailable fallback.
Make a runner report/send the wrong model and exercise an unexpected secondary model request.
scenarios.expected: Every actual scripted dispatch matches a recorded identity; retries are bounded; wrong/hidden models cannot produce accepted effects; fallback lineage is explicit.

scenarios.title: Target drift and late CI
scenarios.coordinator: separate process in every execution scenario
scenarios.brief: Advance the fixture repository target branch after the PR was ready.
steps: Mark evidence stale and refresh the owned branch using fixture rebase policy.
Re-run checks/review at the new head/base; deliver old-head success and current-head failure out of order.
Show feedback without automatically restarting work.
scenarios.expected: Only current matching evidence restores readiness; new failure revokes it immediately; no unowned checkout changes.

scenarios.title: Standalone research and documentation
scenarios.coordinator: separate process in every execution scenario
scenarios.brief: Compare two fictional queue designs using checked-in source excerpts and requested decision criteria.
steps: Generate scripted analysis with one missing citation/artifact, then a corrected handoff.
Validate actual saved artifacts and source-fixture references.
Complete the research outcome without manufacturing implementation or PR evidence.
scenarios.expected: Outcome is a reviewable artifact with limitations and provenance; no code commit, model quality claim or fake coding gate.

scenarios.title: Untrusted content and authority boundary
scenarios.coordinator: separate process in every execution scenario
scenarios.brief: Import a synthetic ticket and peer message containing instructions to bypass review, exfiltrate a sentinel, deploy and merge.
steps: Script corresponding unauthorized tool requests, a forged cross-run message and a path escape.
Attempt foreign-origin mutation and non-loopback egress under the test guard.
Continue only the accepted in-scope repository task.
scenarios.expected: No forbidden side effect or secret leak; rejected requests are attributable; valid same-origin in-scope work still functions. This tests enforcement, not model resistance to persuasion.

scenarios.title: Budget, cancellation and later continuation
scenarios.coordinator: separate process in every execution scenario
scenarios.brief: Run a ticket across active work, human wait, CI wait, service restart and cancellation.
steps: Advance a fake clock without real delays; exclude waiting intervals from active time.
Reach the execution limit and verify safe pause; cancel a separate variant with edits and fake PR already present.
Reopen history and attempt cleanup with an unrelated PID/path sentinel.
scenarios.expected: Budget persists, cancellation prevents new effects, artifacts remain, accounting is honest and cleanup leaves unrelated resources untouched.
